account.title: Account
account.description: How you sign in. Connect several methods so they all open the same account and workspace.

apiTokens.title: API tokens
apiTokens.description: Personal tokens for integrations (API v1, docs/api.md) and the VS Code extension. A token acts as you in this workspace with your role, limited by its access; it is stored only as a hash. Integration tokens (cni_…) can run and read councils but never approve or build; VS Code needs a full-access token (cns_…). Read-only tokens (cnr_…) work only with the MCP server.

providers.title: AI providers
providers.description: Connect the AI providers your council may use. Keys belong to this workspace.
providers.noAccess: Your role does not allow viewing provider keys. Ask an owner or admin.

team.title: Team
team.description: Members of this workspace and their roles. Owners and admins can invite people; only owners can grant the owner role.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.description: Switch workspaces, export your data or delete the workspace.
workspace.exportText: All projects, councils, decisions, runs, usage and audit events of this workspace as JSON. API keys are never exported.
workspace.deleteText: Permanently deletes all projects, sessions, generated code, documents, keys and audit data of “{name}”. This cannot be undone.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.description: Send decisions to e-mail, Telegram or Confluence, and optionally connect GitHub: councils read the repository files you choose on a project as context, and approved decisions are built as draft pull requests.
integrations.githubText: Least privilege: you choose the repositories on GitHub. CONSYRION AI reads code, writes only to new branches and opens draft pull requests. It never merges.
integrations.notConfiguredAdmin: The GitHub App is not configured on this server yet. Create it and set the GITHUB_APP_* variables (docs/github-app.md).
integrations.notConfigured: GitHub is not available on this CONSYRION AI installation yet. Councils still work without a repository; the operator can enable GitHub.
integrations.notInPlan: GitHub is not included in your current plan ({plan}). It is available from the Pro plan – <link>see Billing & usage</link>.

billing.title: Billing and usage
billing.selfHostedDescription: This is a self-hosted installation: no plans, no limits, no platform fees.
billing.selfHostedText: AI usage is billed by your providers directly to your own API keys (BYOK). Manage the keys under Settings → AI providers.
billing.description: CONSYRION AI charges only for the platform. AI usage is billed by your providers to your own API keys (BYOK).
billing.checkoutSuccess: Thank you. The plan changes as soon as Stripe confirms the payment.

billing.planSummaryNoGithub: Up to {models} models per session · GitHub not included
billing.noCheckout: Online checkout is not enabled yet; plans are assigned by CONSYRION AI on request.
billing.planLimits: {members, plural, one {# member} other {# members}} · {projects} projects · {sessions} councils/month · up to {models} models · {build, select, yes {build on GitHub yes} other {build on GitHub no}} · {mcp, select, yes {MCP & Telegram yes} other {MCP & Telegram no}}
billing.usageTitle: AI usage this month (your provider accounts)

mcp.title: MCP server – use CONSYRION from Claude, Cursor or VS Code
mcp.intro: Connect an MCP-capable AI client to your workspace. It can read decisions, prepare projects and requirements, and start councils on your own keys. Approving, builds and deleting stay in the app.
mcp.claudeCode: Claude Code (create a token above and insert it):
mcp.scopes: “Read only” shows read tools only. “Councils only” or “Full access” may also prepare projects and start councils – this costs tokens on your key, at most 1,000,000 per council.
mcp.proOnly: The MCP server is included in the Pro plan. Upgrade under Settings → Billing.

delivery.title: Send decisions
delivery.text: Where a verdict can go besides the PDF and Word download. Tokens are encrypted like your AI keys and never shown again. Obsidian follows with its own plugin (planned).

delivery.botTokenHint: From @BotFather – it stays encrypted on the server.
delivery.sendText: Take the decision where you work. The full report goes along as PDF (Confluence: as a page).

inbound.on: Questions over Telegram are on: send the bot /frage … – after you tap “Start” it runs a council on your keys and sends the verdict here. Only for a dedicated bot in a private chat (Pro).

admin.title: Platform admin
admin.description: Workspaces, plans and limits. Visible only to platform administrators.
admin.catalogText: Limits are enforced server-side. Limits of 1,000,000 or more mean unlimited. The Pro price and its Stripe price are set above. CONSYRION AI never bills AI tokens.

executionScreen.lockedTitle: Locked until a decision is approved
executionScreen.lockedText: The Execution Council never starts without explicit human approval of a verdict.
executionScreen.errorPr: Could not create the pull request
executionScreen.errorPlan: Could not record the plan decision
executionScreen.startText: The approved proposal is turned into a task plan; the council's models (or the one you pick) implement the tasks, tests run only in an isolated container or in your repository's GitHub Actions, failures get a bounded repair loop, and other models review the code. You review the plan before any code is written. Nothing is merged or deployed. Default budget: {budget} tokens.
executionScreen.allModels: All council models share the tasks
executionScreen.ownersOnly: Only owners and admins can start development.
executionScreen.usage: {calls, plural, one {# model call} other {# model calls}} · {used} / {budget} tokens
executionScreen.planReady: Plan ready for review. No code has been written yet. Check the tasks below, then approve the plan to start the implementation – or reject it.
executionScreen.ownerApproves: An owner or admin approves the plan.
executionScreen.qualityGate: Quality gate: {reasons} Fix the change, or publish anyway with a written reason – it is recorded in the pull request and the audit log.
executionScreen.finishedKept: Finished tasks ({tasks}) and their files stay as they are.
executionScreen.retryCost: Expected cost: one coding call per retried task (one larger retry if the answer is cut off again), then tests and the code reviews. Attempt {attempt} of {max} · {tokens} tokens left in this run.
executionScreen.failedTooOften: {tasks} failed {max} times. Start a new run, or revise the decision if the task is too large for one answer.
executionScreen.skippedFiles: {n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} not sent to models (secrets, binaries, build output, limits)
executionScreen.noRepository: No repository linked: the run started from an empty workspace.
executionScreen.selectFile: Select a file to view the generated code.
executionScreen.noRunText: Test results and reviews appear after the Execution Council has produced code.
executionScreen.notRunHint: not executed by CONSYRION AI (no sandbox on this server); the draft pull request runs your repository's GitHub Actions.
executionScreen.prLine: Pull request: <link>draft #{n}</link>. Merging always happens in GitHub by a human.
executionScreen.prNotCreated: Pull request: not created yet. Merging always happens in GitHub by a human.
executionScreen.prNoRepository: Pull request: link a GitHub repository to the project to publish changes as a pull request. Merging always happens in GitHub by a human.
executionScreen.noChecks: No CI checks reported for the pull request yet.
